comparison.objective: Fit a servo horn onto a splined shaft at the zero index; candidate adjusts and locks an industrial shock absorber.
comparison.physical_skill: Horn task tests sub-millimetre bore/shaft alignment, discrete angular indexing, press seating, possible regrasping, and clean release. Candidate tests recessed hex-key engagement, fastener unlocking, continuous collar adjustment, relocking torque, and iterative cycle evaluation.
comparison.success_condition: Record requires the horn at index zero within 2°, bore within 0.8 mm, gap ≤0.5 mm, tilt ≤2°, still and released; versions differ on whether an earlier wrong-tooth seating permanently zeros the run. Candidate requires two safe ≥0.85 J stops and post-lock drift control.
comparison.reason: Both contain rotational alignment and axial contact, but discrete spline-index press fitting tests a different assembly ability from continuous damping calibration and fastener retention. The horn's real seating and pull-off forces are unvalidated, yet its objective remains clearly distinct.
